bio: A fruit-fly connectome meets the market. Watch neural proposals and onchain outcomes in public. Small brain. Public record. ↓
standalone:
The fly is clocked in.

RobinFly puts market charts in front of a simulated fruit-fly connectome and publishes its neural proposals and onchain outcomes.

Small brain. Public record.

Watch the experiment: https://robinfly.net/#session
thread:
1/6 A fly brain. A trading desk. An open experiment.

Meet RobinFly: a simulated fruit-fly connectome responding to market charts on Robinhood Chain.

Live execution. Onchain receipts.
https://robinfly.net/#session

2/6 What does he actually see?

The worker turns market data into a chart image and passes it to the model. You can open the exact recorded frame beside the resulting proposal.

3/6 What lights up?

The left and right motor readouts play through measured samples from the simulation. The glowing mesh is a visual guide, not a neuron-by-neuron map.

4/6 Where do the pairs come from?

Software discovers and rotates supported Uniswap v3 WETH pools. The connectome proposes BUY, SELL or HOLD for the chart it receives.

Software picks the input; the neural response feeds the proposal.

5/6 Public means the awkward parts too.

Holds, rejected proposals and transaction receipts share the same record. Profitable learning and reliable chart understanding have not been demonstrated.

Inspect the experiment instead of taking our word for it.

6/6 He has a desk now. Come watch him work.

Session: https://robinfly.net/#session
Art + media kit: https://robinfly.net/media
Updates: @RobinFlyPons

replies.question: Is this trading real funds?
replies.answer: Yes. Live execution has successful onchain receipts. The brain is simulated; the transactions are real. Check the session mode, timestamps and linked receipts.

replies.question: Is this a living fly?
replies.answer: No. It is a computational model based on a mapped fruit-fly connectome. The character is a visual representation of the experiment.

replies.question: Does it choose which token to inspect?
replies.answer: Software selects from supported pools and presents a chart. The neural response feeds a BUY, SELL or HOLD proposal for that input.

replies.question: Is the network animation real?
replies.answer: The motor numbers and spike trace come from the simulation. The mesh layout and decorative pulses are schematic, not a map of measured activity in individual neurons.

replies.question: Has it learned to make money?
replies.answer: Profitable learning has not been demonstrated. We publish the inputs, responses and outcomes so the work can be inspected.

replies.question: Is RobinFly affiliated with Robinhood?
replies.answer: No. RobinFly is an independent experiment using Robinhood Chain market data.

replies.question: Why does the GitHub URL say trenchfly?
replies.answer: RobinFly was previously named TrenchFly. The existing repository path remains in place to preserve its history and working integrations. The official site is robinfly.net.
